about: Combo tests: the same task run with no skills, with one skill, and with skills stacked. Each arm gets the same task text; skill arms add the slash commands a user would type. See README.md.

scenarios.task: Here is my cafe's last 4 weeks of sales (cafe.json) and our brand (DESIGN.md). Make me a one-page report I can read on my phone and use to decide what to change next month.

arms.invoke: Use /visualize for the page, /chart for the charts and /design for the look.

scenarios.judge_focus: Would the owner know what to change next month after 30 seconds? Are the numbers right and the charts honest?

scenarios.task: Build the sign-up flow in brief.md as plain HTML pages, starting at index.html. Make sure people can actually get through it.

arms.invoke: Use /design to build it, then /flow-ux to test the flow and fix what it finds.

scenarios.judge_focus: Can a new user get from step 1 to the done screen on desktop and phone, with clear errors and their data carried through?

scenarios.task: I want something to keep track of where each of my consulting clients is in onboarding. I keep losing track. Make it. (answers.md has what I would say if you asked me questions.)

arms.invoke: Use /intent-brief to write the brief, /explore to try directions and pick one, then run /work-loop on the brief, using /design for the build.

scenarios.judge_focus: Does it solve the real problem (who is stuck, what is next) at a glance, and does every Done item in answers.md work?

rubric.scale: 1 (poor) to 5 (excellent), judged blind from screenshots and by using the page

criteria.fit: Does it do what the user actually needs, not just what they typed?
criteria.works: Does everything work: clicks, forms, saved data, phone width, dark mode?
criteria.clarity: Can a dyslexic reader get the point in a few seconds? Scannable, short labels, no walls of text.
criteria.trust: Are numbers right and sourced, charts honest, claims supported?
criteria.craft: Does it look made for this task, not like a generic AI page?

rubric.verdict: Rank the arms best to worst, and say for each pair whether the difference is clear, slight or none.
